open_points.subject: _authorize_project_operation
open_points.text: _authorize_project_operation: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST authorize a service principal from persisted state, never from the actor value it was handed. Inside the same open transaction it MUST read the stored principal and reject through the concealment boundary when that principal is absent or not active, and when the stored principal's scope_mode is the GRANTED_PROJECTS member of = models.ProducerScopeMode it MUST also read that principal's grant for this project and raise the scoped not-found rejection when the grant is absent or not active. Those reads go through get_service_principal, called with service_principal_id, and get_producer_grant, called with service_principal_id and project_id, of the service_identity repository of that same transaction, a ServiceIdentityRepository. Skipping them authorizes any caller that can name a principal identifier, which is the one inbound machine path the product has.
open_points.other_text: _authorize_project_operation: [DEPENDENCY_BOUNDARY] MUST make each read and write its other notes call for through get_staff and get_staff_session of the staff_access repository of that transaction, a StaffAccessRepository, and through get_viewer and get_viewer_session of the viewer_access repository of that transaction, a ViewerAccessRepository.
open_points.question: Must the dependency-boundary note include service-principal reads through the service_identity repository, or must its claim about each read and write be narrowed to staff and viewer identity/session reads?
